director.chapterArc: A somber, ritualistic transition from grief to survival; the scene moves through a shared labor of burial, a stark philosophical exchange about loss and utility, an identity revelation that is deliberately flat, and concludes with a long, wearying journey where small physical sensations anchor the emotional weight.
director.restraintNote: Maintain Toren's internal arithmetic as a coping mechanism; Rook's dialogue must remain clinically detached even when discussing death or pain. Avoid melodrama in Milo's grief or Senna's stoicism. The 'warmth' returning to Toren should feel physical and small, not magical.

cues.delivery: Measured, rhythmic delivery for the arithmetic of labor; Toren's counting is a physical anchor.
cues.through: They carried the stones from the scree at the foot of the west wall, two hands at a time, a hundred and forty yards each way. Toren made thirty-one trips. He knew the number exactly, and after the eleventh trip the number was the only thing keeping his legs going.
cues.reason: Establishes the ritualistic nature of the work and Toren's internal state.

cues.delivery: Flat, declarative listing; treat each name as a fact of logistics rather than an emotional eulogy.
cues.from: Garrick Voss, forty-four years old, of Sallow Creek.
cues.through: And a gray mule, because Milo said in a small flat voice that he was not going to leave him lying in the traces. Nobody argued. It took four extra trips.
cues.reason: Reflects the group's utilitarian approach to grief and burial.

cues.delivery: Senna's voice is dry paper texture; precise, authoritative but gentle. No rising inflection on questions.
cues.from: Senna sat against the bank with the blanket around her and gave directions about the stones, which was the only work anyone was going to let her do and which she did with total seriousness.
cues.reason: Establishes Senna as the matriarchal anchor and reinforces her stoicism.

cues.delivery: Rook's voice is flat and low; no edges. The admission of not knowing her must sound like a factual observation.
cues.through: Then he walked off down the road toward the cut, and left them there, and Milo Faust put his hands over his face and finally, four hours late, made a sound.
cues.reason: Highlights Rook's utilitarian philosophy regarding sacrifice.

cues.delivery: Rook's response is clinical and unemotional; the contrast between Toren's grief and Rook's logic must be sharp but not shouted.
cues.through: "In two days this'll be off the road and up in the scrub and gone. In two days it's worth nothing at all." He moved four feet up the gutter. "Today it's worth about nine weeks of what your grandmother's going to need at the far end of this road, and I am not going to stand in a gutter and pretend otherwise so that a thirteen-year-old can have a better afternoon."
cues.reason: Establishes the power dynamic: Rook as the harsh mentor.

cues.delivery: Dessa's question is direct; Rook's answer 'Rook' must be delivered with absolute stillness and no inflection.
cues.through: "I know," Rook said. "You've all been saying each other's names at each other for four hours."
cues.reason: The identity reveal requires a pause for the name to land as a fact.

cues.delivery: Rook's voice is flat and rhythmic like reading a bill; the decision to go north must sound inevitable.
cues.from: He laid it out after the food, flatly, the way a man reads a bill.
cues.reason: Reinforces Rook's role as the tactical leader making hard choices.

cues.delivery: Toren's internal monologue is analytical and cold; the 'emptiness' should feel physical.
cues.from: He knew where it was now. That was the awful part — he could find the spot exactly, the way you can find a tooth that has come out, and there was nothing in it. Not cold. Not dead. Just a small quiet emptiness where, thirty-two hours ago, there had been a warm coin.
cues.through: He reached anyway. He pulled at it with everything he had until his eyes went hot. Nothing happened. Nothing kept on not happening for a long time.
cues.reason: Conveys Toren's grief through sensory description rather than emotion.

cues.delivery: Toren's 'I hate you' is conversational and quiet; Rook's responses are flat acknowledgments.
cues.from: "It went out," he said. "On my father. At the end. It went out and it didn't come back and he —"
cues.reason: The confrontation must feel like a cold exchange of facts between two exhausted people.

cues.delivery: Narrative observation only; the silence of Rook's decision must be heavy and still.
cues.from: Toren did not move. He lay with his cheek on his arm and watched a man decide something.
cues.through: If he said anything, Toren did not hear it.
cues.reason: Builds tension through inaction and Toren's watchful perspective.

cues.delivery: Toren's physical sensation of the Ember returning is small and quiet; Rook's reaction is a micro-movement.
cues.from: On the third afternoon it came back.
cues.through: But Toren was watching for it by then, and he saw the man's chin come up half an inch at exactly the moment the metal ran, and go back down again, and nothing else about him move at all.
cues.reason: The return of power must feel like a subtle shift in reality.

pauses.reason: Completed thought; pause for the weight of 'cairns' to land.

pauses.after: And a gray mule, because Milo said in a small flat voice that he was not going to leave him lying in the traces. Nobody argued. It took four extra trips.
pauses.reason: Speaker reset/paragraph turn; shift from listing names to Senna's dialogue.
Completed thought; pause for the subtext of 'I know you know' between Toren and Senna.

pauses.after: "I'm no good at this," he said. "It isn't going to sound better in a year."
pauses.reason: Speaker reset/paragraph turn; Rook's admission requires a beat before he walks away.
Major emotional landing; the revelation of 'collecting them' (the ash) needs time to register as horror/utility.
Prepares for the emotional weight of Toren's grief.
Emphasizes the utilitarian value Rook places on the ash.

pauses.after: "I didn't ask you that." The man kept holding it out. "Your father put eleven of them down in a gap eight feet wide. That woman held off about forty by herself. The boy with the chain took a leg off one and the one with the bar broke six that I can read from the pattern on the ground." He pushed it into Toren's hands. "That's not mine. It was never going to be mine. Don't lose it, and don't let anybody at a gate see how much of it you've got."
pauses.reason: Speaker reset/paragraph turn; shift from Rook's instruction to the group eating at dusk.
Sets up the tactical decision making.
Major emotional landing; 'I'm going that way' is a commitment of survival and direction.

pauses.after: He reached anyway. He pulled at it with everything he had until his eyes went hot. Nothing happened. Nothing kept on not happening for a long time.
pauses.reason: Speaker reset/paragraph turn; shift from Toren's internal struggle to Rook's sudden appearance.
Isolates the source of Toren's pain before he speaks it aloud.
Major emotional landing; the silence after 'No' is heavy and final for this exchange.

pauses.reason: Speaker reset/paragraph turn; shift from Toren's observation to Rook's micro-reaction.
